topics.label: Introduction to cancer biology and lecture series overview
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the course structure, audience, and core learning outcomes for the lecture series.

topics.label: Cellular and developmental basis of cancer and in vitro models
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how cancer arises from genetic, epigenetic, and differentiation defects disrupting three-dimensional tissue architecture and the experimental limitations of studying these processes in culture.

topics.label: Tumor invasion, metastasis, and distinction from benign encapsulation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how malignant tumors invade through basement membranes and disseminate to distant organs compared to encapsulated, non-invasive benign tumors.

topics.label: Benign-to-malignant tumor progression and nomenclature
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the stepwise transition of benign precursor lesions into malignant tumors and establish the standard histological naming conventions used to classify them.

topics.label: Mechanisms of cancer morbidity and mortality
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic describes the physiological and systemic mechanisms by which primary and metastatic tumors cause clinical illness and patient death.

topics.label: Cancer incidence across human populations and multicellular species
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics compare the epidemiological frequency of different tumor types in humans with tumor incidence across companion animals and other multicellular taxa.

topics.label: Clinical presentation and cancer screening strategies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover early clinical warning signs of cancer and assess the utility and limitations of population screening programs for cervical, colorectal, breast, and prostate cancers.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and upcoming practicals
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session with a recap of learning outcomes and practical session reminders.
